text:
amanda: FYI support ticket #6321 — ACME complaining about 2x latency and burst 429s on their dedicated pool since ~06:10 UTC. They send 100rps steady and we're dropping throughput.
linh: forwarding logs from customer. they see repeated 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED and occasional 503s. Token usage looks normal. They said this started after a config tweak yesterday.
amanda: customer says no config changes on their side. Ticket includes traces and a few example request ids: req_0a1, req_0a2.
jorge: oncall — can you paste the pool id and the reserved capacity? also any recent rolls or runtime flags changed last 24h?
tyler: pool is rpool-acme-eu-west-1, 4xA10g reserved. I see a deploy at 03:50 UTC that toggled scheduler quantum to 8ms -> 4ms for an experiment (cookie: scheduler-alpha). Reverting on canary by 04:30 but maybe some nodes stayed alpha.
ravindra: interesting — early changes lowered max_batch_tokens from 4096 -> 2048 for the canary to improve latency. That could cause more small microbatches and reduce throughput.
linh: customer trace: short prompts but many tokens per response. They usually pack into 6-8 request batches; now we see majority of batches of size 1-2 and small token windows.
amanda: is there an alert for queue depth or batch efficiency?
sre-bot: alert: continuous-batcher:pack_efficiency_drop pool=rpool-acme-eu-west-1 at 06:12 UTC -> efficiency 0.32 (baseline 0.78). peak_queue_depth=4300
jorge: confirm metrics: batch_efficiency_over_time (last 2h): 0.31 -> 0.35. scheduler throughput dropped 45% while latency p50 rose 2.3x. Looks like packing failure.
tyler: digging into scheduler logs. snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T06:11:32Z] batch_attempt: req=req_0a1 size=1 tokens=512 prefetched=false
[2026-03-17T06:11:32Z] schedule_slot: quantum=4ms, max_batch_tokens=2048, current_window=512
[2026-03-17T06:11:33Z] flush_due_to_quantum
```
This shows the lowered quantum and smaller max_batch_tokens -> frequent flushes.
ravindra: that matches. Lower quantum increases flush frequency; with small prompts it prevents packing. We need to test increasing max_batch_tokens and quantum for this pool. Also check continuous-batcher drain threshold and prefill_min_tokens.
linh: customer also reported billing auth errors earlier but support checked — auth tokens successful; billing API had a transient 502 earlier at 05:40 but unrelated.
amanda: good to rule out billing. Can we reproduce locally with a synthetic load matching their request size distribution?
tyler: repro steps I used locally:
1) run stressgen with 100rps, prompt_size=50 tokens, expected_response=500 tokens
2) scheduler set to quantum=4ms max_batch_tokens=2048
3) observe pack efficiency ~0.33 and 429s at client when queue_depth>2000
Command:
```
./stressgen --rps 100 --prompt-tokens 50 --resp-tokens 500 --duration 10m --target-pool rpool-acme-eu-west-1
```
Results attached in the ticket.
jorge: good repro. Suggest rolling scheduler flags back to quantum=12ms and max_batch_tokens=4096 for this pool as mitigation.
ravindra: also propose bumping prefill_min_tokens to 256 and enabling kv-cache-prefill (already on?) to help packing. We can do a canary change on 1 node then roll if stable.
tyler: small run with quantum=12ms locally shows pack_efficiency 0.72 and throughput restored to ~95% baseline. latency p50 back to expected.
linh: customer asked for timeline — can we do the rollback now and notify them?
amanda: support will ask for a maintenance window; but given impact we can schedule an immediate config rollback on dedicated pool controls and label change as mitigation.
jorge: action items:
- tyler: push rollback flag to pool rpool-acme-eu-west-1 (quantum=12ms, max_batch_tokens=4096) — now, canary on 1/4 nodes
- ravindra: prepare metrics dashboard to watch pack_efficiency, queue_depth, p50/p95, error_rate
- linh: notify customer with expected 30min mitigation window and ask for any extra traces
- amanda: escalate to account exec if customer wants credit
tyler: starting canary update. command:
```
infractl pool-config set rpool-acme-eu-west-1 --scheduler-quantum-ms 12 --max-batch-tokens 4096 --canary-nodes 1
```
sre-bot: deploy_event: pool_config_change started pool=rpool-acme-eu-west-1 canary_nodes=1 by tyler at 06:25 UTC
tyler: canary node shows immediate improvement: pack_efficiency=0.69, queue_depth dropped 60% in 2m, no 429s in canary logs.
jorge: if canary stable 10m, roll to rest of nodes. Watch for noisy-tenant interactions — larger batches may increase tail latency for high-priority tenants.
ravindra: add safety: autoscale policy unchanged; if queue_depth spikes >5000 let's auto-scale +1 GPU earlier than usual.
amanda: customer notified: "We observed higher latencies; performing a rollback of scheduler flags — expect improvement within 10-30 minutes. We'll update when rolled out." They replied :thumbsup: and asked to keep them in loop.
linh: monitoring shows overall cluster pack_efficiency climbs to 0.68 after full roll at 06:52 UTC. error_rate down to baseline.
jorge: closing loop — root cause: accidental canary flag bleed (scheduler quantum + lowered max_batch_tokens) -> increased flushes -> small microbatches -> throughput drop. Mitigation: rollback and adjust prefill + autoscale safety.
amanda: filing postmortem draft, assigning to tyler & ravindra for remediation: add automated canary isolation checks and pre-change sim to detect pack efficiency regressions. I'll add to backlog.
linh: ticket updated, customer satisfied. Closing support escalation.
